assessment: The SARS-CoV2 M protein is an abundant protein in the viral envelope and is a potential target for vaccine and therapeutic development. M is one of only four structural proteins that are incorporated into mature SARS-CoV2 virions. This paper describes a single-particle cryo-electron microscopy structure of M in lipid nanodiscs. M forms a dimer similar to the previously characterized SARS-CoV2 ORF3a viroporin, which was proposed to function as an ion channel. Structural analysis and molecular dynamics simulations indicate that, unlike ORF3a, M functions as a structural scaffold protein. The highly charged surface of the M's cytosolic domain suggests how it might interact with other structural proteins and/or the charged RNA genome during virion packaging.
